Borrow Fire, Then Become Fire · 04 / 05

Formation: from human agency to personal philosophy and practice

People enter collaboration with experience, preferences, intuitions, and existing agency. How can these acquire a form that others can understand, use, and revise? This group examines the formation of personal philosophy. Literary programming condenses understanding through characters, imagery, and relationships; metaphor develops through analogy into questions and possible consequences, entering practices distributed across people, models, records, and tools.

Writing a Sinthome then asks how such expression can become a distinctive form that sustains living and creation. Writing, use, and revision return to one another, while established descriptions remain open to experience. Two further readings branch into speech and self-description, and into machines, connections, and becoming.

Essays in this stage

01

Literary Programming

Condense understanding through characters, imagery, and relationships, then unfold it through instructions and tools.

02

Metaphor, Analogy, and Personal Self-Revision

Develop metaphor into analogy and relation maps, distribute cognition across models, records, and tools, and revise that organization.

03

Writing a sinthome: forming a personal philosophy

Begin with a person who already perceives, generates, and acts; expand capacities with models and form a personal philosophy and the environment that sustains it.

Focused branch: Speaking, self-description, and signifying chains

Focused branch: Machines and Becoming: An Encounter with Deleuze and Guattari
